title: SRS carriers: provenance inside the documents people already use

sections.name: claim
sections.label: Claim
sections.content: An SRS repository can travel inside a document people already open, so the document still reads as itself and an SRS reader also gets everything behind it: the transcript, the data it was enriched with, the topic map, the sources. This is the first practical line of third-party adoption: SRS as a way to enhance data, and still usable. The owner, 2026-11-27: "This is probably the first line of practical third party adoption. SRS as a way to enhance data ... And still usable."

sections.name: story
sections.label: The story so far
sections.content:
Two prototypes on 2026-11-27 put a whole SRS archive inside a PDF/A-3, as an associated file marked /Source, with a small binding in the PDF's metadata (repository, composition, archive and rendering checksums). A separate reader finds the payload, checks it, re-renders the composition from it and compares with what was printed.

Meeting minutes worked end to end: the page reads as minutes; the payload carries a transcript, a calendar enrichment, three topics pointing at transcript cues, and the relations from topics to the decision and tasks.

The muSrs essay Rebuilding Small Democracy worked with features SRS already has: a boundary container whose childContainerIds are the essay and its references, exported as an RFC-026 slice (155 records, 7 source documents), and a composition that prints each paragraph's sources under it. The page is 26 pages; the record is the evidence.

The weak points are not in the idea. A PDF re-saved through ordinary tools loses its payload silently; a checksum binding catches drift but not a determined forger; SRS has no stored digest for source documents (srs#1053); and some rendering and slice behaviour gets in the way of a clean published page.

sections.name: parts
sections.label: The parts
sections.content:
1. The idea: carriers, formats and design rules.
2. Prototype: meeting minutes in a PDF.
3. Prototype: a muSrs essay, sliced at its boundary.
4. Trust: binding the page to its record.
5. What SRS needs: bugs and gaps found.

sections.name: open
sections.label: What is open
sections.content: Three exercises: which carriers SRS should define and how a reader finds the payload; how a reader trusts that a page matches its record; where an essay's publication boundary should live. Not yet done: veraPDF validation, a signed carrier, an HTML carrier, and a user outside the programme. The working group label wg:third-party-ready exists for this.

sections.label: Finding the evidence
sections.content: Findings: srs find --type com.semanticops.programme/finding --tag topic:carriers. Exercises: srs find --type governance/exercise --tag topic:carriers. Where the prototype code is: part 2.
